concerns.concern: The pressure-induced side dips, which are the main evidence for pz dominance and for excluding B1u, may be thermal or critical-current artifacts. The heating test uses only ambient-pressure data, which have no dips.
concerns.quote: conductance dips outside the gap are the textbook signature of the thermal/critical-current regime... No test is applied to the pressurized spectra, where the dips actually appear.

concerns.concern: The fitted gap magnitudes give 2Δ/k_BTc of about 12–13. That is roughly four times weak coupling and far above STM gap scales. The fitted Δ therefore likely absorbs non-spectroscopic broadening, which undermines the meaning of the gap ratio.
concerns.quote: A fitted "Δ" this large most likely absorbs non-spectroscopic broadening, such as heating, spreading resistance or multiple parallel contacts.

concerns.concern: There are too many free parameters for the spectral content. Several spectra are single featureless peaks only 5–15% above background, which cannot constrain a gap ratio together with Z and Γ.
concerns.quote: Such a shape cannot constrain both a gap ratio and Z and Γ.

concerns.concern: Au is excluded using simulations with Γ = 0.01 meV. The fitted Γ of about 0.4 meV would wash out the peak splitting that is used to rule Au out.
concerns.quote: The fitted Γ ≈ 0.4 meV at ambient pressure exceeds the simulated gap, and would wash out the peak splitting that is used to exclude Au.

concerns.concern: B1u is excluded only because side dips are absent, yet the ambient S1 and S2 spectra also show no side dips.
concerns.quote: B1u is excluded only by the absence of side dips, but S1 and S2 at ambient pressure show no side dips.

concerns.concern: Quantitative model comparison is missing. The review requests fits with all IRs and an s-wave baseline at equal freedom, χ² or information criteria, covariances, a statement of which parameters were fixed (Z and Γ look constant at all T), and the sensitivity of the superposition fits to the number of components.
concerns.quote: best fits with Au, B1u, B2u/B3u, and an s-wave/BTK plus broadening baseline, all with the same parameter freedom, together with χ² or an information criterion

concerns.concern: A change in Δz/Δx(y) within a single IR is not fixed by symmetry. It therefore does not by itself show that SC1 and SC3 are distinct phases, especially since both may be B3u.
concerns.quote: Δz/Δx(y) within a single representation is not fixed by symmetry and can vary continuously with pressure.

concerns.concern: The proposed B2u → B3u transition is thermodynamically non-generic, since a mixed state would be expected. Also, B2u and B3u give identical (0 0 1) spectra in the authors' model, so it is unclear why a B3u onset would produce a minimum in the ratio.
concerns.quote: A second-order transition below an existing B2u state into a different IR normally produces a mixed state (B2u + B3u or B2u + iB3u), not a replacement.

concerns.concern: The minimum in the ratio might come from fit-parameter trade-offs, since error bars are very large near Tc. A simulation of a two-IR state is needed to show it reproduces the minimum.
concerns.quote: show that the minimum cannot arise from fit-parameter trade-offs... near Tc both gaps are small and the error bars are very large

concerns.concern: The basic junction characterization is not reported: R_N at each pressure, contact radius, comparison with mean free paths, and the dI/dV measurement scheme. Without these, bulk series-resistance contributions cannot be ruled out.
concerns.quote: These are needed to establish whether the series bulk resistance of the sample contributes.

concerns.concern: All pressure data come from one Au-epoxy junction that was compressed and thermally cycled. The fitted Z and Γ change substantially, which indicates the junction itself evolved.
concerns.quote: The fitted Z (1.67 → ~1.2) and Γ (0.39 → 0.10 meV) change substantially... which indicates that the junction itself evolved.

concerns.concern: The authors should test whether the dip bias scales with R_N or stays at fixed voltage, give the field dependence of the dips under pressure, and state whether the 1.4 GPa spectrum is in the thermal regime.
concerns.quote: show whether the dip bias scales with R_N (expected if V_dip = I_c R_N) or stays at fixed voltage

concerns.concern: The claimed abrupt increase in the ratio rests on about seven pressures from one junction. Denser points near 0.3 GPa or a second junction are needed.
concerns.quote: The "abrupt increase" in the Fig. 5a inset rests on about seven pressures from one junction, with Z and Γ also changing.

concerns.concern: Only one contact on one sample was measured under pressure. The main trends (side-dip onset, ratio minimum, double dips) need reproducing on a second contact or sample, or in a pressure-release run.
concerns.quote: Only one contact on one sample was measured under pressure.

concerns.concern: The authors should state whether each pressure point required warming to room temperature and how the contact changed after thermal cycling.
concerns.quote: Please also state whether each pressure point required warming to room temperature, and how the contact changed after thermal cycling.

concerns.concern: The BTK model assumes a spherical Fermi surface and linear-in-k gaps. UTe2 has quasi-2D cylinders with small v_z and lattice-harmonic kz-odd gaps, which alters channel weighting and the extracted ratio.
concerns.quote: These differences directly affect the weighting of channels in the k∥ sum of Eq. (1), and hence the extracted Δz/Δx(y).

concerns.concern: The model does not consider the large Fermi-velocity/mass mismatch between Au and heavy-fermion UTe2.
concerns.quote: The large Fermi-velocity/mass mismatch between Au and heavy-fermion UTe2.

concerns.concern: The (0 0 1) surface was polished rather than cleaved, and its roughness breaks the specular-reflection assumption of the model.
concerns.quote: The polished (non-cleaved) (0 0 1) surface, where roughness breaks specular reflection.

concerns.concern: Non-unitary or chiral pairing combinations proposed in the literature (for example B3u + iAu) are excluded by assumption.
concerns.quote: Non-unitary or chiral combinations proposed in Refs. 16 and 24–25 (for example B3u + iAu), which are excluded by assumption.

concerns.concern: Inferring px(y) dominance from a small peak amplitude (G_NS < 1.2) ignores the generic suppression of Andreev signals in heavy-fermion point contacts and parallel normal channels. The ambient conclusion leans heavily on this argument.
concerns.quote: neglects the strong suppression of the Andreev signal generic to heavy-fermion point contacts

concerns.concern: The normalization of G_NS to G_N and the background used at each pressure are not stated.
concerns.quote: The normalization of G_NS to G_N, and the background used at each pressure, should be stated.

concerns.concern: Field dependence could discriminate B2u from B3u via Zeeman coupling but is not exploited. The existing 8 T, H ∥ a data showing no splitting should be analyzed, and measurements with field under pressure are suggested.
concerns.quote: The existing 8 T, H ∥ a data at ambient pressure (Fig. S2a) show no splitting. This should be analyzed within an extended model including Zeeman coupling.

concerns.concern: The double-dip spectra are attributed either to multiple gaps or to pressure inhomogeneity. These physically different interpretations are not distinguished.
concerns.quote: These two interpretations are physically very different and are not distinguished.

concerns.concern: Pressure calibration is missing: the manometer, the pressure at low temperature versus at loading, and the pressure gradient. These determine whether domain superposition is plausible.
concerns.quote: The Methods give no: manometer (Pb or Sn Tc, or ruby); pressure at low temperature versus at loading; estimate of the pressure gradient.

concerns.concern: The 1.4 GPa spectrum near the magnetic-order boundary is shown but neither fit nor discussed. Magnetic-scattering zero-bias anomalies need to be addressed there.
concerns.quote: The 1.4 GPa spectrum, near the MO boundary, is shown but neither fit nor discussed.

concerns.concern: The ambient resistive transition is unusually broad, and the ZBCP tracks the resistive onset rather than bulk Tc. The origin of the onset, whether the annealed polished surface has a different Tc, and a plot of PCS onset versus pressure are requested.
concerns.quote: The ZBCP appears at about 2.5 K (Fig. 2c), i.e., it tracks the onset rather than bulk Tc.

concerns.concern: Possible interfacial reactions between Au and Te (gold tellurides) are not discussed.
concerns.quote: Possible interfacial reactions should also be discussed, since gold tellurides exist; avoiding Ag does not remove all Te-reaction concerns.

concerns.concern: The non-monotonic Δx(y)(T) at 0.8 GPa, rising between 0.5 and 1.1 K, should be discussed.
concerns.quote: Note the non-monotonic Δx(y)(T) at 0.8 GPa: it rises from 0.87 to 1.00 meV between 0.5 and 1.1 K (Fig. S8).

concerns.concern: The claim of unambiguously demonstrating a pz component is overstated given the concerns about the dips, fit uniqueness and gap magnitudes.
concerns.quote: "Unambiguously suggesting the presence of pz component" is overstated given concerns 1–3 and the authors' own caveat about Au.

concerns.concern: The Table S1 column headers appear swapped. The listed values contradict the figures and the quoted ratio of 0.57.
concerns.quote: Table S1 column headers appear swapped.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 5d caption gives 0.3 K for the 0.8 GPa fit, but the Fig. S8 temperature series starts at 0.5 K. It is unclear which spectrum enters the Fig. 5a inset.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 5d caption gives T = 0.3 K for the 0.8 GPa fit, but the temperature series in Fig. S8 starts at 0.5 K.

concerns.concern: The claimed strong violation of the BCS prediction in Fig. S2c refers mainly to gap magnitude. The normalized Δ(T)/Δ(0) shapes should be compared.
concerns.quote: "strongly violate the BCS prediction" refers mainly to magnitude, not functional form.

concerns.concern: The Fig. S9 caption should define Δ¹ and Δ² and the weights used at 1.2 GPa.
concerns.quote: Fig. S9 caption should define Δ¹ and Δ² and the weights used at 1.2 GPa.

concerns.concern: The SI has formula errors: the k_F expression and a missing parenthesis in the Fermi function exponent. The normal-state-conductance normalization in Eq. (1) and Eq. (S12) should be made explicit.
concerns.quote: "k_F² = √(2mε_F/ħ²)" should be k_F = √(2mε_F)/ħ

concerns.concern: There are reference errors (the Ref. 1 journal name and the Ref. 24 year) and typos in the text.
concerns.quote: Ref. 1 journal name ("Pep. Rrog. Phys."); Ref. 24 year (should be 2020)

concerns.concern: The raw dI/dV data and fitting code should be deposited so that fit uniqueness can be assessed.
concerns.quote: the raw dI/dV(V, T, p) data and fitting code would materially help assess fit uniqueness; please consider depositing them.
